D10·k4n8 — 2026-09-16
rule: Never apply a second, different Seatbelt profile inside a sandboxed process, and never put a symlinked path form in a profile — realpath every entry — and treat a `sandbox_apply` failure as "no isolation", never as a deny.
chose: D9 §9 REVISED (the evaluator's own kernel sandbox is dropped) and two measured Seatbelt facts fixed into the evaluator. Measured 2026-09-16 on macOS 27.0 with /usr/bin/sandbox-exec: (a) a profile can be applied inside an existing sandbox ONLY when it is byte-identical to the one in force — outer `(allow default)` with any different inner profile, or any two different profiles in either order, fail with `sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted` (exit 71); identical text nests fine. (b) Profile paths match the RESOLVED vnode path only: an entry naming `/var/folders/…` never matches a write that reaches `/private/var/folders/…`, while an entry naming `/private/var/folders` matches writes spelled either way. Consequences built: the evaluator process is not re-exec'd under a holdout-denying profile (it would break every candidate, pack and score sandbox inside it, which is exactly how the first controls run recorded `build_failed` for both reference and skeleton); the holdout stays unreachable by the candidate through its kernel profile, and by the evaluator through test/holdout.test.ts, which pins that every mention of the sealed path in evaluator source is a deny-list entry, a probe target or the definition. Every path is realpath'd before it enters a profile. The self-test judges a probe from exit code AND what it left behind, and a `sandbox_apply` failure is reported as "could not be applied" for every probe rather than counted as a successful deny — the first self-test passed ten deny probes vacuously for that reason and was caught only by the one allow probe. The scorer throws (never records a score) when its sandbox could not be applied. The self-test fixture lives on a real path under the evaluator store, not under tmp, which every profile allows.
over: Keeping the evaluator's own profile and applying candidate profiles identical to it (the evaluator must write results the candidate must not); enforcing the holdout ban with chmod (same uid); trusting a deny probe's non-zero exit without checking why it failed.
because: D9 §4 says isolation is measured, not assumed, and the measurement found the mechanism's limits before any launch: nested-apply refusal and symlink-form mismatch. Both are properties of the OS, not of this code, so they belong in the record for every later session that touches a profile. A self-test that can pass while the sandbox was never applied is worse than none, so the allow probe and the apply-failure classification are now load-bearing and unit-tested.
